subject: Art & Design
title: Dark Patterns: Design That Deceives
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dark Patterns: Design That Deceives.

hook.text: 'Unsubscribe' is in tiny gray text at the bottom. 'Stay subscribed!' is a giant green button. That's a dark pattern.

buildup.text: Dark patterns are deceptive UI techniques that trick users into actions they didn't intend: buying, subscribing.

discovery.text: Dark patterns include confirm-shaming, hidden costs, trick questions, and roach motels (easy to enter, hard to leave).

twist.text: The EU's GDPR and California's CCPA now legally prohibit some dark patterns. Regulation is catching up.

climax.text: Amazon's cancellation flow once required 6 clicks and 4 pages. Public backlash and regulators forced simplification.

punchline.text: Dark patterns win clicks. They lose trust. Trust is harder to rebuild.

quiz.question: What is a 'roach motel' dark pattern?
options: Easy to sign up but extremely difficult to cancel or leave
A design that attracts users with fake discounts
A pop-up that appears repeatedly until clicked

details.summary: Dark patterns are deceptive design techniques that trick users into unintended actions — hidden subscription costs, confusing opt-out flows, shame-based decline buttons, and misleading visual layouts. They exploit cognitive biases for business gain at the user's expense.
details.whyItMatters: Dark patterns erode trust, damage brand reputation, and increasingly face legal consequences under consumer protection laws. Understanding them is essential both for avoiding their use and recognizing when they target you as a user.
takeaways: Dark patterns trick users into unintended actions
They exploit cognitive biases for business gain
They erode trust and increasingly face legal consequences

faq.question: What are common examples of dark patterns?
faq.answer: Confirmshaming ('No thanks, I don't like saving money'), hidden costs revealed at checkout, pre-checked boxes for unwanted subscriptions, difficult cancellation flows requiring phone calls, misdirected buttons where the desired action is visually de-emphasized.

faq.question: Are dark patterns illegal?
faq.answer: Increasingly yes. The EU's GDPR restricts manipulative consent interfaces. California's CCPA prohibits dark patterns in privacy opt-outs. The FTC has taken enforcement action against deceptive subscription practices.
